Meaning: System automatically puts policy on hold due to rules linked to agent/broker/channel (e.g., authorization, missing approvals). Broker is not mapped to that product or region → issuance blocked.
Next Steps for Customer Service: Coordinate with agent/broker and inform issue

Meaning: Initial policy booking details (premium, coverage, client data) need verification. Eg Quoted premium ≠ system premium due to wrong exposure value.
Policy is awaiting risk assessment/decision from underwriting. Large liability policy requires underwriter approval before issuance.
Policy cannot be auto-issued; requires manual creation/issuance. Eg. Custom wording or special clauses require manual processing.
Significant mismatch found between declared vs verified exposure data. Eg. Declared payroll ₹2Cr but audit shows ₹3.5Cr → premium gap.
Technical/system error preventing policy processing. Eg. Policy stuck in issuance due to integration failure.
Policy under final quality checks before issuance. Eg. QA team validating premium, endorsements, and wording accuracy.
Policy changes requested before final issuance. Eg. Customer wants coverage increase after booking but before issuance.
Policy data needs validation in EPA (Electronic Policy Administration system). Eg. Policy details not matching system-generated view.
Policy requires region-specific regulatory or system handling. Eg. Policy issued under Canada compliance framework.
Policy depends on master policy setup. Eg. Contractor policy cannot be issued until master OCIP program is finalized.
Placeholder record created; full details not yet entered. Eg. Policy logged quickly to meet deadline but missing information.
Issuance delayed due to system/document inventory or queue restrictions. Eg. Policy stuck due to document sequencing or system batch control.
